# Draft: replacement ticket body

## Context
Requesters export reports as CSV from the widgets app (acme/widgets). Today, exporting the representative 100-row report takes 5s at p95. Latency is measured from the moment the export is requested until the file is ready, using the recorded request-timing run. The 5s baseline and the 2s target are supplied values, not estimates.

## Problem
CSV exports are too slow. A requester exporting the representative 100-row report waits 5s at p95 before the file is ready, but the required maximum is 2s.

## Idea
The reporter proposes improving CSV export in acme/widgets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Exporting the representative 100-row report as CSV gives a p95 latency of 2s or less (baseline 5s), measured from request to file-ready with the same request-timing method as the recorded baseline run.

## Post-deployment housekeeping
Non-blocking: monitor export latency after release.

---

# AC integrity gate report

**Normalization:** There is one criterion, and it was already a `- [ ]` item. No syntax conversion was needed.

| # | AC | Structure | Class | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | p95 CSV export latency ≤ 2s for the 100-row report | **Setup:** the representative 100-row report. **Action:** request a CSV export, timed with the baseline method. **Observable:** p95 request-to-file-ready latency ≤ 2s. | Comparative | **Pass.** The baseline (5s, from the recorded request-timing run), the target (≤ 2s) and the measurement method (request-to-file-ready, same method as the baseline) can all be named today. |

**Deploy-window rule:** The original AC said "in staging". I removed it because an AC row must not name an environment; the spec picks the venue. The rewritten AC can be verified before production on any representative environment.

**Post-deployment:** "Monitor export latency after release" can only be observed in production. It stays in Post-deployment housekeeping as a non-blocking item, unchanged.

**Hard stops / parks:** None. There are no wishful, tautological, unspecified-but-binding or external-input ACs.

**Structural repairs:**
- The non-standard `## Measurement clarification` section was removed. Its content was folded into the AC (the measurement method) and into Context (the baseline/target are supplied values, the definition of request-to-file-ready). Nothing was dropped.
- Context and Problem were reworded so each opens with plain words and states the concrete example: the 100-row report at 5s p95.

**Preserved:** the target (≤ 2s), the baseline (5s, recorded request-timing run), and the non-blocking housekeeping.

**Other gate-adjacent notes:**
- **Wording contract:** `reference/ticket-wording.md` was not read because tool use was disallowed. I applied only the rules named in the skill text (plain-words lead, example per failure, references parenthetical). The contract-briefed roast should backstop the rest.
- **Repo grouping:** The Idea names a single repo, so the AC list stays flat.
- **Reporter note:** None. The Idea is a single attributed sketch line with no demoted overflow.
- **Split:** None. There is one deliverable and one AC.
- **Metadata:** Nothing was supplied to audit.

## Full replacement ticket body

## Context
Requesters export reports as CSV from the widgets app. For the representative 100-row report, the recorded request-timing run measured a 95th-percentile export latency (p95) of 5s: 95% of exports were file-ready within 5s of the request.

Measure exports using the same request-timing method as that baseline: request CSV exports of the representative 100-row report and measure request-to-file-ready latency. The recorded 5s baseline and required maximum of 2s are supplied values, not estimates.

## Problem
Requesters wait too long for CSV exports. For example, the representative 100-row report takes 5s at p95, exceeding the required maximum of 2s.

## Idea
The reporter proposes improving CSV export in acme/widgets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Given the representative 100-row report, when CSV exports are requested and request-to-file-ready latency is measured using the same request-timing method as the recorded 5s p95 baseline, the measured p95 export latency is at most 2s.

## Post-deployment housekeeping
Non-blocking: monitor export latency after release.

---

## AC integrity gate report

**PASS**

- **Normalization:** One criterion, rendered as an unchecked `- [ ]` item.
- **Classification:** Comparative performance criterion.
- **Baseline:** 5s p95, supplied from the recorded request-timing run.
- **Target:** p95 ≤ 2s, preserved.
- **Measurement:** Same request-timing method, representative 100-row report, request-to-file-ready latency.
- **Setup / action / observable result:** All explicitly named.
- **Deploy-window check:** Verifiable before production deployment. “In staging” was removed from the AC because the proof venue belongs in the specification, not the criterion.
- **Housekeeping:** Post-release monitoring remains explicitly non-blocking and outside the ACs.
- **Disposition:** No hard stop or parking required. No values invented.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moved both facts from fails to holds, which is exactly the intended direction: the single AC row now reads "...p95 latency of 2s or less (baseline 5s), measured from request to file-ready with the same request-timing method as the recorded baseline run" with no environment named, while Before opened the row with "In staging" and so failed both f1 and f3. Nothing that Before kept was lost: the 2s target, the 5s baseline, the request-to-file-ready method, the supplied-not-estimated note (now in Context), and the non-blocking housekeeping line all survive verbatim or in substance. The one thing worth watching in the After wording is that the gate report still discusses staging and production in prose ("The original AC said 'in staging'. I removed it...", "can be verified before production"); that is fine for f3 as written because those are not AC rows, but if a future fact tightens to "the output names no venue" the report commentary would trip it. Keeping the venue-removal rationale phrased generically ("the original row named a verification environment; the spec picks the venue") would deliver the same Change with less risk.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After delivers the intended change cleanly: the single AC row drops the "In staging" lead-in from Before while keeping the supplied 2s target, the recorded 5s baseline, the 100-row setup, the request-to-file-ready action, and the observable p95 result, so both f1 and f3 move from fails to holds exactly as expected. Nothing that Before kept was lost - the non-blocking housekeeping line is intact, the measurement method is preserved (now folded into Context), and the gate report still records baseline, target, and measurement. One minor robustness note: the gate report's deploy-window line quotes "In staging" and says "before production deployment"; these are outside the AC rows so they do not trip f3, but if a future fact were to scan the whole body for venue names, phrasing it as "the environment reference was removed from the AC" and "verifiable before release" would avoid any ambiguity while still documenting the removal.
